text: On the other hand, if one of these unmerciful talkers lays hold of you, hear him with patience (and at least seeming attention), if he is worth obliging; for nothing will oblige him more than a patient hearing, as nothing would hurt him more than either to leave him in the midst of his discourse, or to discover your impatience under your affliction.
author: Philip Stanhope, 4th Earl of Chesterfield
locator: Letter LIV, to his son, Bath, October 19, Old Style 1748
